query: What additive manufacturing strategy and post-processing route can enable the fabrication of a refractory high-entropy alloy family (Group IV-V transition metals) capable of retaining high-temperature structural integrity, and what specific microstructural state is hypothesized to optimize mechanical performance while mitigating the inherent brittleness associated with interstitial impurities?

generation.hypothesis: A refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) based on the Group IV-V transition metal system (Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V) fabricated via Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) using pre-alloyed powders, followed by a stepwise thermo-mechanical processing route involving hot rolling and dual-stage aging, will yield a microstructure containing coherent δ-lamellae and γ″-type nanoprecipitates that mitigate interstitial-induced brittleness while retaining high-temperature structural integrity.
generation.material_initial_state: LPBF-fabricated Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V alloy with a single-phase BCC solid solution, characterized by elemental segregation (W enrichment in grains, V depletion), sub-grains (~500 nm), and spherical V-rich precipitates at boundaries, resulting in inherent porosity and brittleness due to interstitial impurities and rapid solidification defects.
generation.intervention: Post-processing via hot rolling (80% reduction at 1200 °C) followed by cold rolling (75% reduction at 25 °C), annealing at 900 °C for 5 minutes, and dual-stage aging at 650 °C for 20 hours to induce stepwise coherent precipitation.
generation.conditions: Processing in high-purity argon atmosphere to minimize interstitial contamination; aging temperatures selected to stabilize coherent precipitates without coarsening; testing at ambient and elevated temperatures (up to 800 °C).
generation.structural_mediator: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) consisting of ~40 nm wide δ-lamellae (D0a structure) and ~10 nm spheroidal γ″ particles (D022 structure) sharing a coherent interface with the BCC matrix.
generation.mechanism: The coherent interfaces of the δ-lamellae and γ″ particles facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, preventing premature crack initiation associated with interstitial impurities and grain boundary segregation. The lamellar boundaries and particle pinning provide synergistic strengthening (solid solution, grain boundary, and order hardening) while maintaining ductility through strain hardening.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy will exhibit an ultimate tensile strength exceeding 2.0 GPa with tensile ductility >10% at ambient temperature, and retain a yield strength >1.0 GPa at 800 °C, significantly outperforming the as-printed state which suffers from porosity-induced brittleness and lower strength.
generation.baseline: As-printed LPBF Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V alloy with 95% density, 1391 MPa compressive strength, and brittle failure modes due to porosity and unmelted particles, or arc-melted counterparts with coarse grains (25 µm) and lower strength (1107 MPa).
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies specifically to Group IV-V transition metal RHEAs (Nb, Ta, Mo, W, V) where high melting point differences cause segregation; it assumes the availability of pre-alloyed powders to mitigate initial segregation and requires the specific dual-stage aging to form the coherent precipitates.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty exists regarding the specific solubility limits of interstitial elements (O, N) in the Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V system during LPBF and whether the specific aging parameters (650 °C) will successfully nucleate the δ and γ″ phases without forming brittle topologically close-packed (TCP) phases, as the base LPBF study noted significant elemental segregation and impurity issues.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V RHEA via LPBF using pre-alloyed powders, apply the proposed hot rolling and dual-stage aging (900 °C/5 min + 650 °C/20 h), and compare microstructure and mechanical properties against a control sample processed only by LPBF and standard solution annealing.
measurements: TEM/STEM analysis to quantify volume fraction, size, and coherence of δ-lamellae and γ″ precipitates
Uniaxial tensile testing at room temperature and 800 °C to measure UTS, yield strength, and elongation
Fractography analysis to identify failure modes (ductile vs. brittle/cleavage)
APT analysis to assess interstitial distribution and segregation at precipitate-matrix interfaces
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the aged samples fail to form coherent δ-lamellae and γ″ precipitates (as evidenced by TEM/APT) or if the mechanical testing shows a decrease in ductility (<5% elongation) or strength (<1.5 GPa UTS) compared to the as-printed state, indicating that the aging route induces brittleness rather than mitigating it.

Question: Can refractory high-entropy alloy WTaMoNbV be adequately synthesized via a laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process using mixed elemental alloying powder as the raw material, and how do its properties compare to a counterpart produced by arc melting furnace (AMF)?. System: Refractory High-Entropy Alloy WTaMoNbV (20 at.% W, 20 at.% Ta, 20 at.% Mo, 20 at.% Nb, 20 at.% V). Processing: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) using EOSINT M290 system (400 W Nd-YAG laser, pure argon atmosphere); mixed elemental powders (20–70 µm) stirred for 6 h at 23 rpm; advanced trials parameters: 244 W laser power, 300 mm/s scanning speed, 0.10 mm hatch spacing, 0.03 mm layer thickness, 162.7 J/mm³ energy density, 67° layer rotation.. Test conditions: Density and Vickers hardness (HV10) measured; compression strength tested at 0.5 mm/min crosshead speed; electrochemical behavior assessed via potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5% NaCl solution at ambient temperature (scanning rate 0.5 mV/s)..
